description: §17.6.4 / §17.6.2 — the value-form sugar at a BOUND (binding-site) position with NO trailing `else`. The `else` is OPTIONAL; when no arm executes the binding receives `not`, which renders as NOTHING. `#out-hit` selects the true arm ('YES'); `#out-miss` selects no arm and renders empty. `#out-cascade-hit` pins that an `else if` cascade with no trailing `else` still selects a matching arm (@n is 5, so 'mid'); `#out-cascade-miss` pins that falling off the end of such a cascade binds `not` and renders empty. This is the bound-position twin of ctrl-022, which pins the same two halves in a markup interpolation.
rationale: §17.6.4 is unambiguous on BOTH halves: "An if-as-expression without an `else` arm SHALL have an implicit false-path type of `not`" and "The compiler SHALL NOT emit an error or warning for a missing `else` arm. Missing `else` is valid; the consequence is a `T | not` result type." §17.6.2 supplies the value for the TRUE path without a `lift`: "An if-as-expression arm body SHALL produce its result value via a `lift` statement, **or** by being exactly one expression, which is sugar for `lift` of that expression." Before the fix the true path was the broken one, not the false path: the sugar arm minted a fresh `let _scrml_tilde_N = "YES";` instead of writing the enclosing result var, so the binding was `null` on BOTH paths — `#out-hit` rendered empty exactly like `#out-miss`, at exit 0 with zero diagnostics (g-value-form-sugar-in-bound-position-emits-null). The false path was already correct and is pinned here so the fix cannot over-reach: `not` is the seed the result var is initialised to, and it must SURVIVE an unselected cascade. The absence assertions are the other half of §17.6.4's ruling — no diagnostic of ANY severity may be raised for the missing `else`, so E-CTRL-/E-LIFT- are excluded by prefix and W-LIFT-001 (which has no emit site in compiler/src at the time this case was written) is excluded by name as a forward guard.
